name: Keyboard hint
description: A keyboard key or shortcut hint drawn as a small keycap: in help text, menus, tooltips and search fields, with platform-specific modifier adaptation (macOS ⌘/⌥, Windows Ctrl/Win, Linux Super) and international layout awareness.

classes.ayy-kbd: The <kbd>: monospace, 0.75em of the surrounding text, a hairline border with a heavier bottom edge.

default.looks: A small keycap: wash fill, line-strong border with a 2px bottom edge, mono text-soft at 0.75em.

hover.none: A key label, not a control.

pressed.none: A key label, not a control.

disabled.none: A key label, not a control.

selected.none: A key label, not a control.

sizes.density: Scales with the text around it (1.6em tall); scales when surrounding text uses --ayy-text-s.
sizes.width: At least 1.6em wide, grows with the key name.

js: kbdClass and keyboardHintClass constants. platformKeyLabel(key, platform) maps modifier names to platform symbols/names ("mod" → ⌘ on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux; "meta" → ⌘ on Mac, Win on Windows, Super on Linux); platformKeyName(key, platform) gives its spoken name ("Command" for ⌘).

props.keyName: string — a modifier or key drawn for the platform ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift", "enter", "backspace"). Symbols get an aria-label with the key's name. The server and first render draw Windows names, then the user's platform.
props.platform: "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

props.keyName: string — optional modifier/key name to adapt ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift")
props.platform: "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

a11y: Use the <kbd> element: screen readers and search know it's a key.
Write modifier names out where symbols may not read well ("Ctrl" rather than "^"), or add aria-label="Command K" to a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (screen readers pronounce "⌘" as "place of interest sign").
A shortcut hint doesn't replace aria-keyshortcuts on the control it triggers.
do: Use a kbd for keys people press: "Press / to search", shortcuts in a menu or tooltip, a hint in a search field (InputGroupAddon).
Use one kbd for a whole shortcut (⌘K), or one per key with a plus between them (Ctrl + Shift + P).
Adapt modifiers to the user's OS: ⌘ / ⌥ / ⇧ / ⌃ on macOS, Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Win on Windows, and Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Super on Linux (or use <Shortcut keys="Mod+K" /> / <Kbd keyName="mod" />).
Listen to event.code (physical key like 'KeyE') or use matchShortcut(event, 'Mod+E') rather than event.key === 'e' so hotkeys work across keyboard layouts and languages (e.g. Russian Cyrillic Cmd+У).
dont: Don't use a kbd for code or file names — use .ayy-mono or <code>.
Don't use it as a badge or a tag — use Badge.
Don't show shortcuts on touch-first screens, where there's no keyboard.
Don't hardcode Mac-only symbols (⌘) or Windows-only names (Ctrl) when targeting multiple operating systems.
Don't check event.key for letter shortcuts: on non-Latin keyboard layouts (e.g. Russian ЙЦУКЕН), event.key produces localized characters ('у' instead of 'e') and the hotkey fails silently.
